text: Mai was stirring a big pot of soup when she remembered her sister's message. She dried her hands and said to her phone, "I'm sorry to bother you, but could you please find the picture I took of grandmother's soup last winter and send it to my sister Lian? She wants to cook it for her birthday, and she has lost the recipe, so I would like her to see all the herbs on top." The phone searched her album and found a photo with a close view of the bowl. It asked, "Should I send it as a message?" Mai said yes. A moment later the phone said, "Done. I sent the photo to Lian." Mai thanked it, and a fraction of a minute later her sister answered with three hearts. Mai smiled and went back to her pot.

The person wants calm music to start while they bake a cake on a chilly afternoon.
play something calm
put on some quiet music, please
music, something slow
can you start a relaxing playlist
it's so quiet in the kitchen, I could use a little tune
I'd love some soft songs while I bake
the house feels empty without a song
Could you put on something gentle? I'm going to be baking for a long while and I like to hear music while I work.

The person wants to restart the computer. A new update rang its little bell, and the bread recipe on the screen can wait.
restart now
reboot it
turn it off and on
please restart the computer
my laptop is stuck, can you reboot it
start over, please
Could you shut the computer down and start it up again? It has been slow all day and I would like a fresh start.

Person: I need to go to the post office on the way to work. Can you find the nearest one?
Assistant: Sure. Do you want the one near your home or near your office?
Person: Near my office. Actually, no, near the kids' school. I drop them off first.
Assistant: Got it. The post office on Mill Street is two minutes from the school. It has good parking at the back.
Person: Great. I need to send a parcel, but the box has a funny design, so it might be too big.
Assistant: I can't measure your box, but I can read you the biggest size the post office takes. Do you want that?
Person: Yes please.
Assistant: The biggest box is sixty centimetres long. Yours should fit if it is shorter than that.

Moshe had only just moved to the city, and his new flat still felt empty. There was a bed, a table, and one drawer full of papers. His cousin Dina was coming to visit, but there was no room for her. Moshe said to his phone, "Please book a hotel room for my cousin. She is staying eleven nights, and it should be near the train station." The phone asked, "How many guests?" "Just one," said Moshe. It found a small hotel two streets from the station and booked a room for eleven nights. Then it said, "Your cousin can check in after three o'clock." Moshe decided to draw a little map on a card, with the hotel marked in red, and put it in the drawer to give to Dina.

Victor was a student, and his friends were coming for dinner in one hour. He had a bag of chicken pieces and no idea what to do. He asked his phone, "How long do I cook chicken in the oven at two hundred degrees?" The phone said, "About twenty-five minutes." Victor wanted to skip the long step of making a sauce, so he asked, "Will it still be tasty with only salt and lemon?" The phone said it would, and read out a short list of steps. Then Victor said, "Set a timer for twenty-five minutes." The phone started the timer and said the total time to dinner would be about forty minutes with the rice. Victor laughed and began to cut the lemon.

Ravi hated being late. It was a hot day, and the heat made everything slow. His daughter had a loose tooth and a dentist visit at four. Ravi picked up his phone and said, "Book me a ride to the dentist on Park Road for half past three. I don't want a long wait, and I don't want a car without a child seat." The phone asked, "Where should the car pick you up?" "At the front gate," said Ravi. The phone found a car with a child seat and booked it. It said, "Your driver will be there at three twenty-five." Ravi told his daughter to put her shoes on. She wiggled her loose tooth the whole way down the stairs.

name: remove_news_topic
does: Wipes a topic out of the person's news feed so those stories stop showing up.
inputs: the topic to remove, like snowy weather reports or the Sunday sports page
people say:
- I'm sick of hearing about celebrities, stop showing me that
- no more weather stories in my news please
- take football out of my headlines
- I don't want to see election stuff anymore
- hide everything about cars from my feed

Giulia was a student who had slept only four hours, and her face felt heavy. She had a quick drive to the lake to see friends. Before she left, she asked the car assistant, "Do my tyres need more air?" The assistant checked and said, "The front left tyre has less air than the others, about half a bar lower." Giulia stopped at the petrol station near her house. She said, "Remind me what the right pressure is." The assistant said, "Two point three bar." She filled the tyre until the number matched. Then she said, "Where did I park last time at the lake?" The assistant showed a spot on the map. Giulia drove off, hoping she could sleep well that night.

name: translate_food_label
does: Translates the words on a food package into the person's language, so a sick or allergic person can check what is inside, and says if the item is past its date and should go in the bin.
inputs: a photo of the package or the words on it, and the language to translate into
people say:
- what does this label say, it's in Italian
- can you read the ingredients on this tin for me
- is there milk in this? the box is in German
- I can't read this packet, what's in it
- tell me what this Japanese sauce bottle says

Person: Wake me at six tomorrow and play some soft music.
Assistant: Sure. Should the music get louder slowly?
Person: Yes, slowly. I have a huge meeting at eight and I need to sleep well.
Assistant: Do you want the lights off at a certain time tonight?
Person: Ten o'clock. I work late sometimes, and my brother's van is loud outside, so use quiet music.
Assistant: Okay. Lights off at ten, soft music at six, getting louder slowly. Should I also check your calendar for the meeting?
Person: No, thanks, I know the time.

Bread rises because tiny yeast eats sugar and makes bubbles in the dough. People let the dough sit in a warm place, and some even set the bowl in a bath of warm water. On a cloudy, cold day it rises slowly, so it may need more time. The recipe says how long to bake and at what heat, and most people follow it closely. When they want a change, they say things like bake it ten minutes longer, make the oven hotter, or set a timer for forty minutes. Others ask for a darker crust or a softer loaf. A kitchen assistant can set the timer, change the oven temperature, or read the next step out loud.

A thermostat tells the heating when to start and when to stop. It checks how warm the room is and turns the radiator on if the room is too cold. A small electric heater may glow red when it is working. People change the temperature a few degrees at a time, and they use words like warmer, a bit cooler, or set it to twenty. Some ask for the heating to come on before they get home, or to stop at night. When a room feels cold, they might say it's chilly in here, and a smart thermostat can turn the heat up. It saves energy to heat only the rooms you use.

name: save_pickup_spot
does: Saves a pickup place so the next ride can start from the same spot, such as the corner by the pepper market.
inputs: a name for the spot, like home or work, and the street address or the last place you were picked up
people say:
- remember this corner for next time
- use the same pickup place as last time
- put my work entrance down as a regular spot
- save where I got picked up, it was easy to find
- next time pick me up at the back door of the mall

The person wants a single birthday message sent to a friend at midnight.
send Anna happy birthday at midnight
text Anna at twelve tonight, it's her birthday
wish Anna a happy birthday as soon as it's the new day
I need a birthday note to go to Anna while I'm asleep
Could you send Anna a nice note when the clock hits twelve?
message Anna right when her birthday starts
Please send a birthday message to my friend Anna exactly at midnight, because I will be asleep by then and I never want to be the last one to wish her well.

Aminata had a cough and a final report due next Tuesday at noon. It was late, and the office was getting dark. She did not want to get up and walk to the wall. She said to her desk lamp, "Make the light warmer and a little brighter, please." The lamp changed to a soft yellow and grew brighter. After a while her eyes were tired, so she said, "Dim it to half at this point, and turn the ceiling light off." The assistant dimmed the lamp and switched off the ceiling light. Then Aminata said, "Turn everything off at nine." The assistant answered, "I will turn the lamp off at nine tonight." Aminata coughed, drank some tea, and kept typing.

when is the chicken done

A phone camera takes a photo when you tap the button, and the picture is saved in an album. People take pictures of friendly faces, food, and trips, and keep them for a long time. Sometimes you chill on the sofa and look at old photos for a while. People change small things, like making a photo brighter, cutting off the edges, or moving it to another album. They also share photos with others. To ask for these changes, people say things like take a picture, show me my last photos, send this one to Mum, make it brighter, or put these in the holiday album. A phone assistant can do all of this by voice.

Person: It's so quiet in here. I'm bored.
Assistant: Would you like me to play some music?
Person: Yes! The song about the round moon.
Assistant: I know a few songs about the moon. Which singer do you mean?
Person: I don't remember. I'm just a kid, I only know the tune. It goes la la la.
Assistant: I can't find a song from a tune alone, but I can play songs about the moon one at a time. Should I start?
Person: Okay. Wait, can you make it louder? I can't hear the click of the drum.
Assistant: Sure, I turned it up a little.

Counting days helps people look forward to things. A child may want to know how many days are left until a sweet birthday cake, and a parent may count how many weeks remain before school. People also count things, like how many chairs are in a room or how many rugs are in a shop. They ask in simple ways: how many days until Friday, how old is my dog, how many sleeps until the party. A phone can count for you. Some people even tweet a countdown to tell their friends. When a date changes, they say, make it the twentieth instead, and the count starts again.

Music can be changed in simple ways. Volume says how loud a song is. When you boost the sound, it gets louder, and a bass boost makes the low notes stronger. Some speakers let you pan the sound to the left or the right, so you hear more from one side. People want music to sound clear in a big room or a small car. They say things like turn it up, a bit quieter, skip this song, play the next one, or put on some jazz. They also ask for a playlist, or for the same song again. A speaker assistant listens for those words and changes the music right away.

Tane was a gardener, and his sister's birthday was coming. He was kneeling by the roses when he remembered. She had a constant love of flowers, so he wanted a gift that matched. He wiped his hands and said to his phone, "Remind me to call my sister at half past six tonight, and find me a link for a nice rose bush I can send her." The phone replied, "I will remind you at half past six." Then it found a shop and read out two choices. Tane chose the red one. The phone said, "I will schedule the delivery for her birthday." Tane smiled and went back to his roses, and at half past six his phone rang with the reminder.

Wolfgang was not good with technology. His son had put cameras around the house, but Wolfgang never knew how to use them. He was going away, and his bike was in the garage, so he worried. He said to the speaker in the kitchen, "I'm going away by the end of the week. Can you try to turn on the cameras at night, and tell me if anyone comes near the garage?" The speaker said, "Yes. The garden camera and the garage camera will turn on every night at ten. I will send a message to your phone if they see someone." Wolfgang asked, "Will the local police know?" The speaker said, "No, only you will get the message. Do you want me to add your neighbour?" Wolfgang said yes, and went to pack.

Assistant: I can't cut the intro, but I can play at one and a half speed. Do you want that?

Lamps and ceiling lights make a room bright. A smart bulb can change both brightness and colour. A narrow lamp shines on a desk or a book, while a ceiling light fills the whole room. At night, a small light helps a baby who cries or a puppy that cries in the dark feel safe. People change lights with words like brighter, dimmer, turn it off, make it warmer, or make it blue. They may say it's too dark in here when they want the light on. With a voice assistant they can ask for the kitchen light, the lamp by the bed, or all the lights at once.

Tendai was a grandparent, and their grandson was playing football for the first time on Saturday. Tendai could not go to the field, so they picked up the phone. "I would be very grateful if you could tell me the score of the Blue Hawks match," said Tendai, "because my grandson plays for them, and I am so proud of him that I cannot wait." The assistant said, "The Blue Hawks are winning, two to one." Tendai wrote the score on a card with a pen and asked, "Can you send him a message too?" The assistant said, "Yes. What should it say?" Tendai said, "Wave a big hello from Grandpa, and say well done." The assistant sent it right away.

Max was a driver on his lunch break, parked near a market. His friend, a teacher, had asked him to bring dessert, so he decided to build a cake with a single layer of cream. He said to his phone, "Give me a recipe for a cream cake with strawberries." The phone read the list of things he needed. Then Max said, "Wait, I mean a cake with bananas, not strawberries. The market has no strawberries." The phone said, "Okay, I changed the recipe to bananas," and sent the new list to his messages. Max bought bananas and cream, and the phone set an oven timer for his evening at home.

name: flood_exit_helper
does: Searches for the safest road out of a flooded area and gives short steps, like belts on and doors locked, so nervous drivers know what to do.
inputs: where the person is and where they want to go
people say:

- which road is dry right now
- there's flooding near my house, where should we go
- help me leave town, I'm scared of the river
- find a way to my mum's that isn't under water

Person: I need to see the dentist. Can you book it?
Assistant: Sure. Which day would you like?
Person: I want to see them every Monday at nine, because of my daily cough.
Assistant: I can only book one visit at a time, and a dentist does not check a cough. Do you mean a doctor?
Person: Oh, yes, the doctor. Just once, next Monday at nine.
Assistant: Do you know your doctor's name?
Person: Dr. Kim.
Assistant: I booked a visit with Dr. Kim next Monday at nine.

inputs: the city or country, even a bitter cold place like Reykjavik
people say:

- is it morning yet in London
- is my sister awake in Sydney
- can I call New York now or is it too late
- how many hours ahead is Paris

name: parking_time_reminder
does: Reminds the person before their parking runs out, so they can unpack the car and still get back in time.
inputs: where the car is parked, when the ticket ends, and the colour of the zone, like purple
people say:
- tell me before my parking runs out
- I only paid for two hours, don't let me forget
- ring me ten minutes before the meter ends
- how long do I have left on the car park ticket
- nudge me when I need to move the car

Person: We went to eat at a cafe and the bill was eighty-four dollars. Can you divide it?
Assistant: Sure. How many people are there?
Person: Three. Me, my wife, and my friend.
Assistant: Okay. Eighty-four divided by three is twenty-eight each.
Person: Wait, I forgot my brother came back to eat with us. Make it four.
Assistant: Four people, so twenty-one dollars each.
Person: Thanks, I'm a student so I have to be careful. Can you also add a tip of ten percent?
Assistant: Yes. The tip is eight dollars and forty cents, so each person pays about twenty-three dollars.

Jing was a cook planning a holiday party for the whole street. Dr. Lee, the family doctor, was coming too, so Jing wanted the house to look nice. Jing said to the phone, "Find me red paper lanterns for the front hall." The phone showed six choices. Jing looked at the prices and said, "These are expensive. Show me ones under twenty dollars." The phone showed three. Jing tried to weigh the cost against the size and said, "Wait, I mean for the garden, not the hall. I need ones that don't get wet." The phone changed the search to garden lanterns and showed two cheap ones. Jing picked one set and said, "Order this one, please." The phone placed the order and said it would arrive on Thursday.

Beatrice was a cook, and while the bread was baking she liked to hear the news. Her hands were full of flour. She said to the kitchen speaker, "Read me the local headlines, please." The speaker read four short stories about a road closing, a new school, a street market, and a storm. Beatrice said, "Actually, I don't want the road news. Just the market and the school." The speaker said, "Okay, I will reduce the list to two stories," and read them. Beatrice also said, "Make it something light, no sad stories today. My grandma used to say a good day starts with good news." The speaker found a story about a dog that rescued a duck, and read it with a smile in its voice. Beatrice laughed.

A storm can cut the power, and then the lights, the heating, and the fridge stop working. People keep a torch, spare batteries, and a charged phone, because a flat phone cannot call for help. When the storm is over and the power comes back, they check the fridge and the lights again. In an emergency, people call the number for help and say clearly where they are. They also say things like call for help, the smoke alarm is going off, is there a flood warning, or when will the storm finish. An assistant can make the call, read out warnings, or switch on a torch light.

name: word_translator
does: Turns a word or short phrase into another language, such as rock, freeze, or grey, and shows how to say it.
inputs: the word or phrase, and the language to translate it into
people say:
- how do you say thank you in Korean
- what's the French word for cold
- I need the Italian for where is the train
- what does gracias mean
- help me say good morning in Swahili

Isabel was a driver who did deliveries, and she needed extra copies of her delivery list. At the print shop, the printer was low on ink. She said to her phone, "See if the printer has enough ink, and print two copies of today's list." The phone checked and said, "The black ink is almost empty. It has less than half left, but I can print two pages." Isabel asked, "Can you print on both sides to save paper?" The phone changed the setting and printed both copies. Then Isabel said, "Look at my calendar and tell me if Friday is free for a new route." The phone said, "Yes, Friday is free all day." Isabel folded the pages and put them in her bag.

Tariq was a shop owner, and the shop was noisy with customers all morning. His cousin in Toronto was going to call, and Tariq did not want to wake the family. He said to his phone, "What time is it in Toronto?" The phone said, "It is five twenty-five in the morning in Toronto." Tariq said, "That is too early. Remind me when it is nine there." The phone said, "I will remind you." While he waited, Tariq took an old receipt and began to draw a sign for the window on the back of it. Later his phone rang softly, and the reminder said it was nine o'clock in Toronto. Tariq picked up the phone and called his cousin.

Pets need food, water, and walks every day. A dog may need a walk in the morning and one in the evening, and a cat may like a bowl of fresh water. On a snowy day, a short walk may be better. Pet owners also go to the vet for check-ups, and they welcome their pets home with a treat. A pet door lets a dog or cat go in and out. People ask for changes with words like feed the cat at six, fill the water bowl, remind me about the vet on Friday, or lock the pet door at night. They may also search the internet for the best food. A home assistant can handle these small jobs.

Victor was a child going camping with his uncle. They needed to pack, and Victor wanted to help. He asked the tablet, "What do I need to bring for a night in the hills?" The tablet gave a list: a tent, a torch, a warm coat, and some food. Victor said, "Can you add more socks? I want double." The tablet put two pairs of socks on the list. Then Victor asked, "Will it be colder than here?" The tablet said, "Yes, about five degrees colder." Victor also asked it to put a card game and some juicy oranges on the list. The tablet said it was done, and Victor ran to find his bag.

When you travel or shop online, prices may be in another currency. The exchange rate tells you how much of one money you get for another. It changes a little almost every day. For a moment, the numbers can make your head swim, so people ask simple questions like how much is fifty euros in dollars, what is the rate today, or is it cheaper to buy it there. A raw number such as one point one means one euro is worth one dollar and ten cents. Some people change money at a bank or a small shop at the airport. Apps and assistants can show a price in your own money quickly.

what time is it in Madrid
Madrid time?
is it late in Madrid yet

Lorenzo was an office worker, and the office was dull and quiet that afternoon. His brother had told him about a fresh episode of a cooking podcast. Lorenzo said to his headphones, "I wish I had something to listen to while I pour my coffee. It's so dull in here." The assistant said, "Do you want me to play a podcast?" Lorenzo said, "Yes, the one my brother likes." The assistant remembered it and said, "I found the cooking show. There is a fresh episode from this morning. I will play it from the start." Lorenzo sat back, sipped his coffee, and listened to a woman explain how to make soup.

sync my contacts

Put my address book on this phone

I need all my friends' numbers here by Friday morning
My old numbers are missing, bring them back
update my contacts with the new numbers on Friday morning
Could you please sync the contact book on Friday morning, when I am home on wifi?

Sanne was a busy parent with a small child on one arm and a bag of groceries on the other. The grass needed cutting, the neighbour had just given a new number for the babysitter, and there was a lot to do. Sanne said to the phone, "Add Mara the babysitter to my contacts. Her number is 555 0142. Don't save it as Mara Smith, she's just Mara." The phone asked, "Should I add her address too?" Sanne said, "No, I don't want her address in the book. Just the number." The phone saved the contact as Mara. Then Sanne said, "Double check the number, please," and the phone read it back. Sanne nodded and carried the bags in.

People use languages to talk with each other. When you learn a new one, you start with words like cage or bird, and with short phrases such as how are you. A translation tool tells you the word in another language, and a spelling tool shows how to write it. A good phrase can last a long time if you say it every day, but if you stop, it may not last. People say things like translate this word, how do you spell it, say it again slowly, or what is the last word in that sentence? Many learners write new words on cards and read them at the end of the day, and the last card is often the hardest.
